reviewed_candidates.reason: The provisional clientRef and final appSessionId are correlated by the sidecar's session.created event; adoption moves only an existing in-memory baseline within the same canonical Git root and does not grant repository or session access.

Provisional baselines use the existing 64-entry bounded cache, successful adoption deletes the provisional key before inserting the final key, and failed session creation therefore cannot cause unbounded memory growth.

First turns are keyed by unique clientRef values rather than a repository-wide fallback, and Last turn lookup accepts only the final appSessionId, preventing one concurrent first turn from replacing another's baseline.

The bridge issues baseline adoption before publishing session.created, but a resulting Review IPC can still race its asynchronous completion. A missing baseline safely falls back to HEAD, and subsequent reads use the adopted session baseline.

Git IPC handlers still lack assertMainRenderer, as documented in the threat model. The new adoption handler only renames bounded in-memory metadata and adds no filesystem mutation or repository access beyond the existing Git IPC surface.
